title: /health must prove a derivation, not just a parse
description:
Final-review finding 2. cloud/factory/src/auth.ts isAuthConfigured() reports auth.configured from parseTokenHash alone, so a record that parses but cannot be derived reports configured:true.

This is the exact contradiction that made the 210k-iteration bug expensive: /health said configured:true while every authenticated request returned 503, which pointed diagnosis at the record's FORMAT when the real fault was crypto. t9k flagged it and correctly left it out of scope.

Fix: have the health path exercise a real derivation (derive against the stored record's own salt and iterations and confirm it completes) rather than only parsing, so 'configured' means 'this deployment can actually verify a token'. Keep it cheap and keep leaking nothing: the response stays two booleans, and a derivation failure must be distinguishable in the LOG from a parse failure, matching the split t9k already added to the middleware.
acceptance_criteria: A deployment whose record parses but cannot derive reports auth.configured:false; a working deployment still reports true; /health still requires no token and still returns only booleans; a test covers the parses-but-cannot-derive case.
